title: Recover the right YARN layer
description: Inject a component failure, set the cluster recovery posture, and choose the first response. The trace distinguishes scheduler recovery from framework retry and from worker-local evidence.

actions.label: Fail over the ResourceManager
actions.detail: Promote the standby and reconstruct scheduler state.

actions.label: Quarantine the worker
actions.detail: Stop new placement and let the application retry lost work elsewhere.

actions.label: Relaunch the ApplicationMaster
actions.detail: Use the application's attempt and checkpoint contract.

actions.label: Correct the container request
actions.detail: Inspect diagnostics, fix the memory envelope, and retry idempotent work.

scenarios.label: Active ResourceManager stops
scenarios.detail: Scheduling and application control lose their active authority.
scenarios.symptom: Node and ApplicationMaster heartbeats cannot reach the active RM.
scenarios.boundary: Promote a standby backed by a healthy state store, then reconstruct applications, requests, queues, and live containers.
scenarios.evidence: Verify active/standby state, state-store health, node re-registration, queue usage, and application progress.
scenarios.correctResult: A standby ResourceManager can resume the control plane. Work-preserving recovery reduces container loss, but the application still must tolerate a temporary scheduling gap.
scenarios.wrongResult: Restarting a worker or one application does not restore the cluster-wide scheduler authority. Applications remain unable to negotiate resources.

scenarios.label: Worker disappears
scenarios.detail: The ResourceManager stops receiving one NodeManager heartbeat.
scenarios.symptom: The node becomes LOST or UNHEALTHY and its running containers vanish.
scenarios.boundary: Stop placing new containers on the node; each framework decides which failed task attempts can be retried on healthy workers.
scenarios.evidence: Check node health, lost container diagnostics, retried task IDs, output commit state, and application progress.
scenarios.correctResult: The scheduler removes the failed node from placement while the ApplicationMaster requests replacement containers. External side effects still need idempotent task design.
scenarios.wrongResult: Failing over the ResourceManager or relaunching every ApplicationMaster expands the incident without removing the unhealthy worker from placement.

scenarios.label: NodeManager process restarts
scenarios.detail: The host remains healthy while its worker agent is restarted.
scenarios.symptom: The NodeManager connection drops, but supervised container processes may still run.
scenarios.boundary: Reload the local NodeManager state store and reattach recoverable containers and auxiliary services before accepting new work.
scenarios.evidence: Verify recovered container IDs, auxiliary-service state, local directories, RPC address, and renewed heartbeats.
scenarios.correctResult: Keep the node out of new placement while recovery reattaches supervised containers. If recovery is disabled, the ApplicationMaster must replace lost attempts.
scenarios.wrongResult: ResourceManager failover cannot recreate NodeManager-local state. Treating the restart as an AM failure leaves the worker boundary unverified.

scenarios.label: ApplicationMaster crashes
scenarios.detail: One application's coordinator loses progress and task state.
scenarios.symptom: The application attempt fails while other applications and nodes remain healthy.
scenarios.boundary: Relaunch the AM within its maximum-attempt policy; the framework restores checkpoints and reconciles already-running or completed work.
scenarios.evidence: Inspect AM diagnostics, attempt count, checkpoint state, container reconciliation, and duplicate-safe output commits.
scenarios.correctResult: The ResourceManager can launch another AM attempt, but the framework defines how much application progress is recovered and which tasks replay.
scenarios.wrongResult: Worker quarantine or cluster-wide failover does not repair an application-specific coordinator and may discard useful running work.

scenarios.label: Container exceeds memory
scenarios.detail: A task crosses its physical-memory resource envelope.
scenarios.symptom: The NodeManager kills the container and reports an exit status and diagnostics.
scenarios.boundary: Measure heap, native memory, overhead, and workload skew; request a justified envelope before retrying the task.
scenarios.evidence: Correlate container diagnostics, stderr, peak memory, host pressure, exit status, and repeated failures by task or input partition.
scenarios.correctResult: A corrected request can stop repeat kills. Keep enough node headroom and investigate leaks or skew instead of only raising every container limit.
scenarios.wrongResult: Changing ResourceManager or NodeManager availability does not correct a task whose process exceeds its declared memory boundary.
